title: Pergamon (Bergama) & Asclepion: Ancient Medical Sanctuary Guide
metaDescription: Visit Pergamon and the Asclepion in Bergama: drive times from İzmir and Ephesus, Acropolis cable car tips, Galen's legacy, and Ayvalık pairing.
quickAnswer: Pergamon sits 105 km (90 minutes) north of İzmir and 190 km (2.5 hours) from Ephesus, making it an easy day trip from İzmir or a smart stop en route to Ayvalık. Ride the four-minute Acropolis cable car, explore the steep Hellenistic theater, then spend 90 minutes at Galen's Asclepion healing complex.
category: Aegean Coast — Ephesus, İzmir, Alaçatı, Bodrum & Pamukkale

body.text: How far is Pergamon from İzmir and Ephesus?

Pergamon—modern Bergama—lies 105 kilometers north of central [İzmir](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/izmir-travel-guide) (about 90 minutes via the O-33 motorway) and roughly 190 kilometers north of Ephesus/Selçuk (2.5 hours by car). While İzmir makes a comfortable same-day base, driving all the way from Ephesus and back in one day leaves too little time for both major ruins.

Public transport is possible via İZBAN north to Aliağa followed by a regional bus to Bergama, taking around 2.5 hours each way. Because the Acropolis, the Red Basilica (Kızıl Avlu), and the Asclepion are spread across three separate sides of town, having a rental car or private driver saves hours of local taxi transfers.
How does the cable car to the Acropolis work?

The [Bergama Acropolis Gondola (Akropolis Teleferik)](https://akropolisteleferik.com.tr/) climbs 694 meters from the lower station on Parmak Batıran Caddesi to the summit entrance in roughly four minutes inside eight-person cabins. It operates daily (typically 08:30–17:00), and its ticket is separate from archaeological admission—your Turkish Museum Pass does not cover the ride.

Check the [official cable car tariff page](https://akropolisteleferik.com.tr/ucret-tarifesi/) before arrival, as foreign-visitor fares are priced separately for one-way and round-trip rides. If strong Aegean winds pause the lift, a paved switchback road lets cars and taxis drive straight to the upper parking lot.

At the summit of this [UNESCO World Heritage site](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1457/), focus your energy on the highlights of the [Bergama Acropolis](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=AKR&SectionId=AKR01):

items: Hellenistic Theater: Seating 10,000 spectators across a dramatically steep slope, it remains one of the steepest ancient theaters still standing.
Temple of Trajan: White marble Corinthian columns restored atop massive vaulted substructures overlooking the Bakırçay plain.

Library & Altar Foundations: View the foundations of the rival library to Alexandria (where parchment—pergamena—gained its name) and the shaded pine terrace where the Zeus Altar once stood before its 19th-century removal to Berlin.

body.text: Why is the Asclepion significant in medical history?

Founded in the 4th century BCE outside the city walls, the [Bergama Asclepion](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=ASK01&DistId=ASK) ranked alongside Epidaurus and Kos as the Roman world's premier medical sanctuary. It pioneered structured whole-body care—combining spring-water hydrotherapy, mud baths, fasting diets, theater therapy, and dream interpretation—and trained Galen of Pergamon, whose pharmacology shaped Western medicine for over a millennium.

Unlike the dramatic cliffside Acropolis, the Asclepion sits on a quiet valley floor framed by olive trees. You enter along the colonnaded Sacred Way (Via Tecta), pass the 3,500-seat Roman theater, and walk through the 80-meter vaulted underground tunnel where patients listened to flowing water and physicians' whispers before sleeping in the incubation chambers. Roman orator Aelius Aristides documented these exact treatments in his Sacred Tales, giving historians rare firsthand records of ancient clinical practice.
Can you combine Pergamon with Ayvalık?

Yes—combining Pergamon with [Ayvalık and Cunda Island](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/assos-ayvalik-cunda) is the smartest geographic move on the North Aegean coast. Bergama sits only 65 kilometers (about 55 minutes) south of Ayvalık, allowing you to tour the Acropolis and Asclepion between 09:00 and 14:30 and still reach Cunda's stone harbor in time for sunset meze.

faq.q: How much time do you need to visit both Pergamon Acropolis and the Asclepion?
faq.a: Plan four to five hours total in Bergama: two hours for the Acropolis (including cable car transit), 90 minutes for the Asclepion, and 45 minutes for lunch or a quick stop at the Red Basilica.

faq.q: Is the Pergamon Altar still in Bergama?
faq.a: No. The monumental Great Altar of Zeus was excavated in the late 19th century and moved to Berlin's Pergamon Museum; only its stone foundation platform remains on the Acropolis terrace.

faq.q: Can you drive up to Pergamon Acropolis instead of taking the cable car?
faq.a: Yes. A paved mountain road climbs around the hill to an upper car park near the Acropolis entrance, which is useful if you dislike heights or if wind temporarily halts the gondola.

faq.q: Are Pergamon Acropolis and the Asclepion covered by one ticket?
faq.a: They are separate archaeological sites on opposite sides of Bergama with separate entry gates, though multi-site regional museum passes cover admission to both archaeological zones (excluding the cable car).

faq.q: What is the best time of day to visit Pergamon?
faq.a: Arrive at the Acropolis at 08:30 opening to avoid midday sun on the exposed marble hilltop, then visit the flatter, partly shaded Asclepion in the early afternoon.

faq.q: Is the Bergama Archaeological Museum worth adding?
faq.a: Yes, if you have an extra 45 minutes in town. Its compact galleries display Hellenistic sculptures, mosaics, and artifacts excavated directly from the Acropolis and Asclepion.
